summary: On paper this one is close: Houston's best edge is to move people pre-snap (Houston ranks 5th in EPA per dropback with motion, +0.12). The model favors Indianapolis at 50%, mostly on home field (1.7 pts) and offensive injuries (0.9 pts).

HOU.detail: Houston ranks 5th in EPA per dropback with motion (+0.12). Indianapolis' defense ranks 14th (+0.08 allowed).

IND.detail: Indianapolis' defense ranks 14th in EPA per dropback with motion (+0.08 allowed). Houston ranks 5th (+0.12).

team_cards.t1: Houston has the 5th-best motion passing game.
team_cards.source: NFLVERSE PLAY-BY-PLAY · FTN CHARTING VIA NFLVERSE

model.summary: Model: Indianapolis 50% to win, fair line IND -0. Market: Houston 53%. The largest factor is home field, worth 1.7 points toward Indianapolis.

model_cards.t1: The model likes Indianapolis more than the market.
model_cards.sub: Win probability. Market = vig-free moneyline at build time.
model_cards.source: NFLVERSE PLAY-BY-PLAY · INJURIES · SNAP COUNTS · SCHEDULES (LINES)
model_cards.note: Not betting advice · market line at build time

model_cards.sub: Each factor's push on the projected margin, in points. Positive = toward Indianapolis. Sum = IND -0.
model_cards.source: NFLVERSE PLAY-BY-PLAY · INJURIES · SNAP COUNTS · SCHEDULES (LINES)
model_cards.note: Linear model, so contributions are exact SHAP values · vs. an average matchup

model_cards.sub: Distribution of Indianapolis's margin. Shaded area = Indianapolis win (50%).
model_cards.source: NFLVERSE PLAY-BY-PLAY · INJURIES · SNAP COUNTS · SCHEDULES (LINES)
model_cards.note: Normal margin, sigma = 12.0 points (fit by log loss)

model_cards.t1: Houston is missing 2.3 starters' worth of snaps.
model_cards.t2: Injuries move the line 1.0 points toward Indianapolis.
model_cards.sub: Players listed Out, Doubtful or Questionable, weighted by recent snap share. QBs are in the QB factor.
model_cards.source: NFLVERSE PLAY-BY-PLAY · INJURIES · SNAP COUNTS · SCHEDULES (LINES)

model_cards.t1: The biggest unit gap: Indianapolis' rush offense.
